metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable web entry point (Struts Action mapped in WEB-INF/struts-config.xml, packaged as a WAR per README) and no sibling service units. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: LoanAction opens a JDBC connection to Oracle and performs an INSERT of business entities (loan applications) carrying user-specific data; no message consumers and no multi-service fan-out.

tech_stack.architecture: Monolithic WAR on Oracle WebLogic 10.3 with direct JDBC to Oracle 11g

findings.title: Documented API Interface
findings.description: The only callable surface is a Struts 1 HTML form action: struts-config.xml maps path '/loan' to com.acme.loan.LoanAction with forwards to quote.jsp and confirm.jsp. No REST controller, GraphQL schema, AsyncAPI spec or RPC service exists anywhere in the repository (searched for @RestController/@Path/servlet REST mappings, *.graphql, *.smithy, openapi.*/swagger.*). Integration therefore requires HTML form posting and JSP screen scraping, or direct Oracle access using the credentials embedded in LoanAction.java.
findings.gap: No machine-callable API. The business logic (amortization calculation and application submission) is only reachable through a browser-oriented Struts action bound to JSP views.
findings.recommendation: Extract the pricing and submission logic from LoanAction.execute into a service class and expose it over a documented JSON/HTTP API (or a facade service in front of the WAR) so agent tools bind to a contract rather than to JSP markup.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Extract the pricing and submission logic from LoanAction.execute into a service class and expose it over a documented JSON/HTTP API (or a facade service in front of the WAR) so agent tools bind to a contract rather than to JSP markup.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Smithy artifact exists. The repository contains 4 files total; the only interface description is the Struts action mapping in struts-config.xml, which describes forwards to JSP pages, not request/response schemas. No spec-generating dependency is present (no dependency manifest at all — README states jars are committed to /lib with no version manifest).
findings.gap: There is no machine-readable contract from which agent tool definitions could be generated; request fields are only discoverable by reading LoanForm getters referenced in LoanAction.
findings.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI 3 document for the extracted loan pricing/submission API and generate it from annotations so it cannot drift from the implementation.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: LoanAction.execute declares 'throws Exception' and saveApplication propagates all JDBC failures unhandled; the only failure path configured is the Struts input attribute input='/loan.jsp', which re-renders an HTML form. There is no error code, error body, or retryable indicator anywhere in the code.
findings.gap: Callers cannot distinguish retriable faults (Oracle connection failure, timeout) from terminal faults (bad input), and errors surface as container HTML error pages.
findings.recommendation: Return structured error payloads (code, message, retryable) from the new API layer and map JDBC/validation failures onto them explicitly.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: The submit path performs an unconditional INSERT INTO applications in saveApplication with no idempotency key, no natural-key uniqueness check and no read-before-write. A repeated submit (agent retry or duplicate tool call) creates a second loan application row. The action is dispatched purely on the form value 'submit' (lf.getAction()).
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism exists for the only write operation in the system.
findings.recommendation: Accept a caller-supplied idempotency key, persist it with a unique constraint on the applications table, and return the original result on replay.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the single write endpoint has no idempotency control.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true (INSERT INTO applications in LoanAction.saveApplication), so agent_scope was inferred as write-enabled and API-Q4 evaluates at its BLOCKER severity.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Accept a caller-supplied idempotency key, persist it with a unique constraint on the applications table, and return the original result on replay.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML: the action returns mapping.findForward('quote') or ('confirm'), resolved by struts-config.xml to /quote.jsp and /confirm.jsp. No JSON or XML serialization code and no content negotiation exist.
findings.gap: Agents would have to parse HTML produced by JSP templates, which is brittle and changes with presentation edits.
findings.recommendation: Emit JSON from the extracted service layer; keep the JSP views as a separate presentation concern over the same service.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission of any kind: saveApplication writes to Oracle and returns; there is no JMS, Kafka, SNS/EventBridge, webhook, or outbox table reference in the repository.
findings.gap: Agents cannot react to loan application submissions or status transitions without polling the database.
findings.recommendation: If event-reactive agents are in scope, add an outbox table written in the same transaction as the application insert, and publish from it.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: The HTTP surface is a WebLogic-hosted Struts action with no throttling: no rate-limiting filter, no gateway in front (deployment is a manual WAR upload per README), and no X-RateLimit/Retry-After headers in the code.
findings.gap: Agent callers have no documented limits and no self-throttling signal; they will discover limits only as connection or Oracle session exhaustion.
findings.recommendation: Document the supported call rate and return rate-limit headers from the fronting gateway once an API layer exists.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application reads request.getRemoteUser() and stores it as the 'officer' column, which implies container-managed (WebLogic) human login, but no authentication configuration exists in the repository: there is no web.xml, no login-config, no security-constraint, no OAuth/mTLS/API-key handling, and no service account definition. The only credential in the repo is a shared Oracle account (DB_USER='loan_app') hardcoded in LoanAction.java.
findings.gap: No machine identity mechanism and no principal attribution for non-human callers; an agent could only call the system by impersonating a loan officer's interactive session.
findings.recommendation: Front the extracted API with an authenticating gateway issuing per-agent client credentials (OAuth2 client_credentials or mTLS), and carry the agent principal through to the persisted record and logs.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Front the extracted API with an authenticating gateway issuing per-agent client credentials (OAuth2 client_credentials or mTLS), and carry the agent principal through to the persisted record and logs.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: There is no authorization model in the repository: no role checks, no permission matrix, no IAM/IaC policies (no .tf/.yaml/CloudFormation present). All database access uses one shared Oracle account 'loan_app' declared in LoanAction.java, so every caller inherits identical, full table privileges.
findings.gap: No mechanism to grant a caller read-only or narrowed access — authorization is entirely coarse-grained.
findings.recommendation: Introduce per-caller scopes at the API gateway and distinct database roles (read-only vs insert) so an agent identity can be granted the minimum needed.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: LoanAction.execute branches on the client-supplied form field lf.getAction(): any caller that reaches the action can trigger the submit (INSERT) path. There is no canRead/canWrite check, no roles attribute on the action mapping in struts-config.xml, and no method-level authorization.
findings.gap: Quote (read-like) and submit (write) operations are indistinguishable from an authorization standpoint — a caller permitted to price a loan is implicitly permitted to create one.
findings.recommendation: Split quote and submit into separately authorized operations and enforce the write permission server-side, not via a form field.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: The only identity handling is request.getRemoteUser() passed as a string into the SQL INSERT. There is no JWT/OAuth parsing, no token exchange, no on-behalf-of flow, and no way to distinguish a caller acting as itself from a caller acting for a loan officer — the officer field is simply whatever the container reports.
findings.gap: An agent acting on behalf of a loan officer cannot be bounded by that officer's permissions, and the audit column cannot separate actor from subject.
findings.recommendation: Propagate a verified token to the service layer and persist both the acting principal (agent) and the subject principal (officer) on every application record.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: Production Oracle credentials are hardcoded as constants in source: DB_URL='jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB', DB_USER='loan_app', DB_PASS='loanApp2010' in LoanAction.java, with a comment noting they are also duplicated in db.properties inside the WAR (README: 'Connection details in a properties file inside the WAR'). No secrets manager, Vault, or rotation mechanism is referenced anywhere.
findings.gap: A static, unrotated production database password is committed to version control and duplicated in the deployment artifact — exactly the kind of secret an agent-facing surface or prompt-injection path can exfiltrate.
findings.recommendation: Move the credential to a managed secret store with rotation, obtain connections from a WebLogic/JNDI datasource instead of DriverManager, remove the constants, and rotate the 'loan_app' password since it is already exposed in git history.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: The only record of a write is the business row itself: the INSERT stores the 'officer' value in the applications table. There is no application log statement in LoanAction.java at all, no logging framework dependency, and no immutable or tamper-evident log store (no CloudTrail/object-lock/retention configuration — the repo contains no IaC). The audit field is in the same mutable table the application writes to.
findings.gap: No immutable, attributable audit trail for loan application creation — a regulated financial write. Forensics on an agent-initiated submission would be impossible.
findings.recommendation: Emit a structured audit event per write (principal, operation, parameters, timestamp, correlation id) to an append-only store with retention, independent of the applications table.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and no immutable audit trail exists for the write path.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true, so agent_scope was inferred as write-enabled; AUTH-Q6 therefore evaluates as BLOCKER rather than RISK-SAFETY. The system also has a write surface, so the dev-library/no-surface INFO calibration does not apply.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Emit a structured audit event per write (principal, operation, parameters, timestamp, correlation id) to an append-only store with retention, independent of the applications table.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No identity lifecycle controls exist: no API key store or revocation endpoint, no service account definitions, and the single database identity is a hardcoded shared account. Disabling a misbehaving caller would mean changing the shared 'loan_app' password or undeploying the WAR, which stops all users.
findings.gap: No way to suspend one caller without taking down the whole application.
findings.recommendation: Issue per-agent credentials at the gateway so an individual identity can be revoked independently of the application deployment.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: saveApplication opens a connection with DriverManager.getConnection (default autocommit), executes a single string-built INSERT, and closes. There is no transaction boundary, no rollback in a catch/finally block (the connection is not even closed on failure), no compensating 'cancel application' operation, and no saga/undo pattern. The submit path also mutates the form (setMonthlyPayment) before writing.
findings.gap: A partially completed or erroneous submission cannot be undone through any supported operation; there is no reversal endpoint and no transactional rollback on failure.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the write in an explicit transaction with rollback and close resources in finally (or try-with-resources after a JDK upgrade), and add an explicit cancel/void operation so an agent-initiated submission can be compensated.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the write path has neither transactional rollback nor a compensating operation.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true and has_http_rpc_surface=true, so the no-write-surface INFO calibration does not apply; archetype is stateful-crud, not stateless-utility, so the archetype downgrade does not apply either.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Wrap the write in an explicit transaction with rollback and close resources in finally (or try-with-resources after a JDK upgrade), and add an explicit cancel/void operation so an agent-initiated submission can be compensated.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: The action supports only pricing (forward 'quote') and creation (forward 'confirm'). struts-config.xml declares no read/list mapping and LoanAction contains no SELECT — there is no way to query an existing application's state, and no status column is written by the INSERT.
findings.gap: An agent cannot inspect whether an application already exists or what state it is in before acting, which also makes retry-safety impossible to establish client-side.
findings.recommendation: Add a read operation that returns application records and their status, so callers can read before write.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency control exists: the INSERT carries no version column, no conditional predicate and no SELECT FOR UPDATE, and no ETag/If-Match handling is present. README explicitly records the known defect 'ActionForms hold mutable shared state; thread-safety bugs under load', and LoanAction's own header comment warns 'Struts 1 Actions are singletons - keep all state local'.
findings.gap: Concurrent callers can interleave on shared mutable form state and create duplicate or inconsistent application rows; the documented thread-safety defect is amplified by machine-speed concurrency.
findings.recommendation: Add optimistic locking (version column / If-Match) on mutable records and verify the Action holds no instance state before allowing concurrent agent callers.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No throttling exists at any layer present in the repository: no rate-limiting servlet filter, no gateway or WAF configuration (no IaC at all), and the HTTP surface is the raw Struts action mapped in struts-config.xml. Each submit also opens a brand-new Oracle connection via DriverManager, so unthrottled calls translate directly into database session pressure.
findings.gap: A runaway agent loop can exhaust WebLogic threads and Oracle sessions, taking down the loan origination path for human officers.
findings.recommendation: Enforce request-rate limits in front of the application (gateway or filter) and use a bounded JNDI connection pool instead of per-request DriverManager connections.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain limits exist. There is no per-caller cap on applications submitted, no principal or APR ceiling enforced in code (the header comment references a 2017 'APR cap' change, but execute() applies no cap — it computes payment from the submitted rate with no bounds), and no bulk-operation or spend threshold.
findings.gap: The business impact of an erroneous agent loop is unbounded: it could submit an unlimited number of loan applications at arbitrary principal and rate values.
findings.recommendation: Enforce configurable per-caller business limits (applications per hour, maximum principal, allowed APR range) in the service layer, independent of request-rate limiting.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: The submit path commits immediately: saveApplication inserts the application row with columns (applicant, principal, rate, term, officer) and no status column, and the action then forwards to confirm.jsp. There is no draft/pending state, no two-step create-then-confirm API, and no approval status in the schema implied by the INSERT.
findings.gap: An agent cannot propose a loan application for human review — any write it makes is final on first call.
findings.recommendation: Add a status column with a PENDING/DRAFT state, have agent-initiated writes land in PENDING, and require an explicit confirm operation to finalize.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval mechanism exists: struts-config.xml exposes a single action with two forwards, there is no approval endpoint, no per-operation configuration flag, and no workflow engine. 'confirm' is a JSP view shown after the write, not a gate before it.
findings.gap: High-risk operations (loan submission) cannot be configured to require human approval at the application layer, so the only possible gate is outside the system.
findings.recommendation: Introduce per-operation approval configuration so submission by a non-human principal requires an explicit human approval call before the record becomes effective.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: README documents 'No unit tests; testing is a shared UAT environment' and deployment as 'Manual WAR upload via WebLogic admin console'. The repository contains no environment-specific configuration, no docker-compose, no seed/synthetic data scripts, and no environment IaC. The hardcoded connection string points at a production host (dbprod01) with no environment switch.
findings.gap: The only test environment is a shared UAT instance with no isolation, no reproducible data shape and no automated provisioning, and the code's default target is production.
findings.recommendation: Provide an isolated, seedable environment with externalized connection configuration so agent behavior can be exercised without touching dbprod01.

Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: the system persists applicant PII and financial data — INSERT INTO applications (applicant, principal, rate, term, officer) in LoanAction.saveApplication, backed by Oracle 11g per README. Stage B1: there is no response scoping of any kind — no DTOs, no @JsonIgnore/write-only serialization, no column projection; the form object LoanForm carries applicant name, principal and computed payment and is handed directly to JSP views. Stage B2: access control is a single shared database account ('loan_app') with no scope differentiation between sensitive and non-sensitive data. Stage B3: no classification metadata — no field-level sensitivity annotations, no tags (no IaC), no Macie/Presidio tooling.
findings.gap: Agent-facing access to applicant PII and loan financials is unscoped and undifferentiated, and the data carries no classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Define response DTOs that expose only the fields an agent needs, split database privileges so PII-bearing columns require a distinct scope, and annotate applicant fields as PII in the schema and code.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: Stage A=Yes (applicant PII + financial records), B1 fired under agent_scope=write-enabled.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Archetype is stateful-crud (not stateless-utility) and the repo is not a dev-library-application, so no INFO calibration applies. B1 fired (no field scoping on agent-consumable responses) which under write-enabled scope resolves to BLOCKER; B2 also fired (RISK-SAFETY) and B3 is absent (INFO). Highest firing sub-check sets DATA-Q1 = BLOCKER.

b1.reasoning: No DTOs, serialization exclusions or column projections; LoanForm with applicant name and loan terms is forwarded directly to JSP views (LoanAction.java:31-45).

b2.reasoning: Single shared Oracle account 'loan_app' (LoanAction.java:22-24); no scopes, roles or row/column-level security differentiate sensitive access.

b3.reasoning: No classification tags, field-level sensitivity annotations, or PII detection tooling anywhere in the repository.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Define response DTOs that expose only the fields an agent needs, split database privileges so PII-bearing columns require a distinct scope, and annotate applicant fields as PII in the schema and code.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The system stores loan applicant PII and financial terms in Oracle 11g on a Solaris host in a single data center (README Architecture section), yet the repository contains no residency or sovereignty controls or documentation: no GDPR/LGPD/jurisdiction references, no region configuration, no cross-border transfer policy, and no data-handling statement. The connection target is a bare hostname (dbprod01) with no region semantics.
findings.gap: Residency constraints on regulated consumer-lending PII are undocumented and unenforced, so there is nothing preventing an agent from forwarding that data to an LLM endpoint in another jurisdiction.
findings.recommendation: Document the jurisdiction and applicable regime for the applications dataset, and enforce an allowed-region/processor policy for any agent or LLM integration that reads it.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the system holds regulated consumer-lending PII with no documented or enforced residency constraints.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_persistent_data_store=true (Oracle via JDBC), so the no-data INFO calibration does not apply, and the archetype is stateful-crud rather than stateless-utility. Under inferred write-enabled scope DATA-Q2 evaluates as BLOCKER.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Document the jurisdiction and applicable regime for the applications dataset, and enforce an allowed-region/processor policy for any agent or LLM integration that reads it.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable for every agent-invoked call to the loan pricing/submission surface.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation exists. LoanForm values are consumed directly: getAnnualRate()/getTermMonths()/getPrincipal() feed the amortization formula with no range or null checks (a zero rate or zero term yields division by zero or NaN), and the applicant name is concatenated straight into SQL — 'INSERT INTO applications (applicant, ...) VALUES ('" + lf.getApplicantName() + "'' — then passed to prepareStatement, so the PreparedStatement provides no parameterization and the endpoint is SQL-injectable. No javax.validation annotations, no Struts validation framework (no validation.xml), and no structured field-level error responses are present.
findings.gap: Malformed or hostile input is neither rejected nor reported per-field; the only write path is open to SQL injection through the applicant name, and numeric inputs are unbounded.
findings.recommendation: Bind parameters with real placeholders (ps.setString/setDouble) instead of string concatenation, add field-level validation with range checks on principal/rate/term, and return structured validation errors identifying the offending field.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: The INSERT writes only (applicant, principal, rate, term, officer) — no created_at, updated_at or event_time column, and no timezone handling or UTC normalization appears anywhere. There are no Cache-Control, freshness or consistency headers because responses are JSP views.
findings.gap: Records carry no timestamps, so an agent cannot determine when an application was created or whether the data it reads is current.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at/updated_at columns stored in UTC and expose them on read responses along with a freshness or consistency indicator.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: There is no logging framework and no log statement in the codebase (no log4j/commons-logging/SLF4J usage in LoanAction.java, no logging configuration file), and consequently no scrubbing or masking layer. Failures instead propagate: execute() and saveApplication() both declare 'throws Exception', so JDBC exceptions escape to the WebLogic container. Because the SQL is built by string concatenation, the exception message carries the fully interpolated statement including the applicant name, which lands unredacted in container logs. .gitignore excludes *.log, so no sample log is available to inspect.
findings.gap: No redaction control exists on the one path that does emit user data — stack traces and SQL text containing applicant PII reach container logs in the clear.
findings.recommendation: Introduce structured logging with an explicit PII masking/allowlist policy, catch JDBC exceptions and log a sanitized message without the SQL text or applicant values.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: A persistent store exists (Oracle 11g applications table) but there is no data quality instrumentation: no profiling report, no null-rate or duplicate monitoring, no freshness SLA, and no quality metrics. Duplicate submissions are structurally possible (see API-Q4), so duplicate rate is both unmeasured and likely non-zero.
findings.gap: Agents reasoning over the applications dataset have no completeness or duplication signal to weigh.
findings.recommendation: Baseline null rates and duplicate rates on the applications table and publish a minimal data quality metric before exposing it to agents.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No versioning or contract artifacts exist: the action path is '/loan' with no /v1/ segment or Accept-Version handling, there are no migration files, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf definitions, no schema registry reference, no changelog, and no CI (so no breaking-change detection or contract tests). README notes dependency jars are committed with 'no version manifest', so even library versions are unversioned.
findings.gap: Any change to the form fields or the applications table is invisible to callers and would silently break agent tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Version the extracted API path, manage the database schema with checked-in migrations, and add breaking-change detection (OpenAPI diff or consumer contract tests) to a pipeline.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Naming is largely self-describing and free of legacy codes: Java properties are principal, annualRate, termMonths, monthlyPayment, applicantName, and the SQL columns are applicant, principal, rate, term, officer. Minor ambiguity exists where names drop units or qualifiers — 'rate' in the table versus annualRate in the form, and 'term' versus termMonths — and no data dictionary exists to resolve it.
findings.gap: No data dictionary documents units (monthly vs annual rate, months vs years) for the persisted columns, leaving room for an agent to misinterpret 'rate' and 'term'.
findings.recommendation: Rename or document the persisted columns to carry units (annual_rate_pct, term_months) so the semantics are unambiguous without a lookup.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No catalog or metadata layer exists: no Glue/DataHub/Collibra reference, no data dictionary file, no schema documentation. The applications table structure can only be inferred from the INSERT statement in LoanAction.saveApplication; README describes the runtime stack but documents no data model.
findings.gap: Teams building agent tools must reverse-engineer the data model from source, slowing tool definition and increasing misinterpretation risk.
findings.recommendation: Publish a minimal data dictionary for the applications table (columns, units, sensitivity) as the first catalog entry for this system.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: Neither tracing nor structured logging is present: no OpenTelemetry/X-Ray instrumentation, no traceparent or correlation-id propagation, and no log statements at all in LoanAction.java. There is no logging configuration file and no logging dependency (the project has no dependency manifest — jars are committed per README).
findings.gap: A failed agent-initiated submission leaves no correlated trace or log record, so it cannot be reconstructed or attributed.
findings.recommendation: Add structured JSON logging with a correlation id accepted from the caller and propagated into the data access path, then instrument with OpenTelemetry.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration exists anywhere in the repository: no CloudWatch alarms or IaC, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, no SLO definitions, no health-check endpoint (struts-config.xml declares only the /loan action). Deployment is manual via the WebLogic console per README, so there is no pipeline-managed monitoring either.
findings.gap: Degradation of the loan path would be detected only by user reports, after agent callers have already begun failing or retrying.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency SLOs for the loan endpoint and configure alerting on them, starting with WebLogic/Oracle metrics already available.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: There is no infrastructure as code: no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, Kubernetes or Ansible artifacts exist (the repository contains only README.md, .gitignore, struts-config.xml and one Java source file). README states deployment is 'Manual WAR upload via WebLogic admin console' on a Solaris host, so the integration surface, credentials and networking are configured by hand with no plan review and no drift detection.
findings.gap: All three sub-checks fail: the surface is not defined as code, changes are not reviewable, and drift is undetectable.
findings.recommendation: Codify the deployment target, datasource and network/auth configuration as IaC under peer review, with drift detection, before exposing the system to agents.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline exists: no .github/workflows, no .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml. The build is Apache Ant with jars committed to /lib (README), and release is a manual console upload. With no pipeline there is also no contract test, no spec validation and no breaking-change gate.
findings.gap: API-breaking changes reach the shared environment with no automated detection, so agent tool bindings can break without warning.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a build pipeline that compiles, runs tests, and validates the published API contract against the previous version on every change.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Rollback is manual and unbounded: deployment is a WAR uploaded by hand through the WebLogic admin console (README), with no blue/green or canary configuration, no feature flags, no traffic shifting, and no retained previous artifact referenced in the repository. The last Solaris host in the data center is the single deployment target.
findings.gap: Recovering from a change that breaks the agent-facing surface depends on a human locating and re-uploading a prior WAR, with no tested path or time guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Keep versioned, immutable build artifacts and automate redeploy of the previous version; longer term adopt blue/green or traffic shifting on a supported runtime.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: There are no tests of any kind: no test directory, no JUnit/REST Assured/Postman artifacts, and README states plainly 'No unit tests; testing is a shared UAT environment'. The amortization formula in execute() and the write path in saveApplication are therefore entirely unverified.
findings.gap: No automated coverage of input handling, output values, or error behavior for the operations an agent would call.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for the amortization calculation and boundary inputs, plus endpoint-level tests for the submit path, and run them in CI.

compensating_controls: Keep the agent out of the submit path (quote-only) until this control exists.
Require human review of every agent-produced loan application before it is acted on.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption-at-rest evidence exists for the Oracle 11g store holding applicant PII: there is no IaC, no KMS or TDE reference, no tablespace encryption configuration, and the JDBC URL 'jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB' specifies no TLS or wallet settings (so the connection is unencrypted in transit as well).
findings.gap: Encryption at rest for the applications table is unverified and uncontrolled from this repository, as is transport encryption to the database.
findings.recommendation: Confirm and document Oracle TDE (or equivalent) for the LOANDB tablespaces and enable TLS on the JDBC connection.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no long-running operations. LoanAction.execute performs an in-memory amortization calculation and a single INSERT; no operation approaches 30s and no job/async framework is present.

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no external service dependencies. The only downstream call is the Oracle JDBC connection in saveApplication; no HTTP/service clients exist.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no priority declared (no additionalPlanContext priority) and no evidence this service is on a declared critical path.

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no list/query endpoints exist. struts-config.xml declares only the /loan action and LoanAction contains no SELECT, so there are no unbounded result sets.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: No metrics or telemetry surface of any kind exists (no metric publication, no dashboards, no instrumentation dependency) — informational absence suppressed per the scoring model; no finding emitted.

items.summary: Create a machine-callable API with machine identity, idempotent and reversible writes, immutable audit, and scoped/classified data access. No agent deployment — including pilots — until these are closed.
Close agent-safety gaps: credential management, authorization scoping, concurrency, rate and blast-radius limits, human-in-the-loop states, and PII handling in logs.
Raise integration quality and engineering maturity: API spec and structured errors, input validation, timestamps, versioning, observability, IaC, CI/CD, rollback, tests, encryption.

recommended_actions.action: Expose a documented JSON API in front of the Struts action
recommended_actions.rationale: Agents cannot bind to JSP screens; every other control needs an API boundary to attach to.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce machine identity and scoped authorization at a gateway
recommended_actions.rationale: Identity must precede data access controls — attribution is currently limited to a container-provided username and a shared database account.

recommended_actions.action: Remove hardcoded production Oracle credentials and rotate them
recommended_actions.rationale: DB_PASS is committed in LoanAction.java and duplicated in the WAR; it is already exposed in git history.

recommended_actions.action: Make the write path safe: parameterized SQL, transaction with rollback, idempotency key, pending state
recommended_actions.rationale: The single write is SQL-injectable, non-idempotent, non-transactional and immediately final.

recommended_actions.action: Add audit, logging and data protection for applicant PII
recommended_actions.rationale: Regulated consumer-lending data is stored with no audit trail, no response scoping, no residency position and no log redaction.

recommended_actions.action: Establish IaC, CI/CD, tests and rollback for the deployment
recommended_actions.rationale: Manual WAR upload with no tests and a shared UAT environment makes any agent-facing change unverifiable and unrecoverable.
